processing_steps: 1. Ingest raw NASA FIRMS CSV files; record per-file manifest.
2. Validate schema, coordinates, timestamps and confidence flags.
3. Normalize: cast types, parse UTC datetime, exclude low-confidence and duplicate rows.
4. Spatial filter: clip to South Sumatra bounding box.
5. Grid assignment: floor(coordinate / resolution) × resolution; points on the upper box edges clamp into the last cell.
6. Monthly aggregation: occupied-cell fraction at 0.25° resolution using Convention B (every cell intersecting the box); Convention A reported as a sensitivity value.
7. Seasonal baseline: per-calendar-month median over baseline window.
8. Anomaly: observed value minus baseline median.
9. Elevated classification: above the 75th percentile of the same calendar month across baseline years.
10. Reliability: repeat classification across all predefined configurations; cross-sensor agreement labels need >= 2 evaluable configurations including >= 1 MODIS and >= 1 VIIRS.

index_definition.name: occupied_cell_fraction
index_definition.unit: fraction of grid cells [0, 1] (dimensionless count ratio)
index_definition.denominator: Convention B: every grid cell intersecting the bounding box (288 at 0.25°, 72 at 0.5°)
index_definition.interpretation_caveat: occupied_cell_fraction counts grid cells (each eligible cell has weight 1, including boundary cells that extend outside the bounding box). It is not area-weighted and is not a burned-area, fire-count or severity measurement.
limitations: Each eligible cell has weight 1; boundary cells partly outside the box count as whole cells.
Cell area varies with latitude; the index is not converted to km2.
Sensitive to grid resolution; tested at two resolutions.
Does not account for differences in sensor detection sensitivity.
Missing months are represented as null, not zero.
Short 2019–2024 baseline (max 6 observations per calendar month).

baseline_window.note: Full available window; declared before analysis.

geographic_support.primary_convention: B: every grid cell intersecting the bounding box
geographic_support.sensitivity_convention: A: grid cells whose lower-left origin lies inside the bounding box

B.eligible_cells: every grid cell intersecting the bounding box

A.eligible_cells: grid cells whose lower-left origin lies inside the bounding box
A.in_bounds_detections: detections in the uncovered boundary strip excluded from the fraction

geographic_support.decision: Convention B approved as primary; Convention A retained as sensitivity comparison (processing version 0.2.0).
geographic_support.note: Convention B includes every in-bounds detection. Its partial boundary cells extend outside the box, so the cells cover more area than the box itself. Convention A covers only cells fully inside the box and leaves a southern strip uncovered. Areas are square degrees, not km2.

scientific_guardrails: Hotspots are satellite thermal-anomaly detections, not unique fires, burned area, severity, ignition causes or fire forecasts.
MODIS and VIIRS records are NOT directly interchangeable.
Common gridding does not equalise sensor sensitivity.
Missing observations are not confirmed zero activity.
Reliability labels are stability measures, not calibrated probabilities of truth.
Harmonization effectiveness has not been independently validated.
